videos.script: Lesson 4 wrote a go.mod with two lines in it, and printed a hint about go mod tidy that nothing used. This lesson is where that hint pays off. {{path}} First the name. A module path looks like a web address, and section 02 shows when it has to be one. The same section reads the versions lesson 1 printed, Docker's odd plus incompatible among them. {{tidy}} Then a dependency. The program from lesson 8 compares two spellings of café, and it needs a module from outside the standard library. One command reads the imports, downloads the module and writes two files. One of those files holds a hash, and a public log checks it before anything is built. You will change one character of it and watch the build refuse. {{vendor}} Last, a copy of the dependencies inside your own module. go mod vendor makes one, the build uses it without being asked, and it costs more than it looks. By the end, every line of a go.mod is something you can explain.
